The '''''Emperor's Will''''' was a [[Star Galleon-class frigate|''Star Galleon''-class frigate]] operated by the [[Imperial Taxation Bureau]] in [[0 ABY/Legends|0 ABY]], at the time of the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]] between the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] and the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Alliance to Restore the Republic]]. That [[Standard year/Legends|year]], the [[Starship/Legends|ship]] set out on a journey to the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Esseles/Legends|Esseles]] with a cargo amounting to 400 million [[Galactic Credit Standard/Legends|credits]] and accompanied by the [[Imperial Navy/Legends|Imperial Navy's]] [[EF76 Nebulon-B escort frigate/Legends|EF76 Nebulon-B escort frigate]] ''[[Zaff Jendinpurg]]''. However, its cargo was [[Capture of the Emperor's Will|captured]] by the ''[[Far Orbit]]'', a Nebulon-B frigate that was acting as a [[Privateer/Legends|privateer]] vessel for the Alliance, on the way to Esseles after the privateers destroyed the ''Zaff Jendinpurg''. The ''Emperor's Will'' was forced to release its ejectable [[Cargo pod (Star Galleon)|cargo bay pod]] in an attempt to get it and the treasure it contained away from the privateers, though the ''Far Orbit'' was still able to capture the pod.

==Description==
The ''Emperor's Will'' was a [[Star Galleon-class frigate|''Star Galleon''-class frigate]] produced by [[Kuat Drive Yards/Legends|Kuat Drive Yards]], and it measured 300 [[Meter/Legends|meters]] in length. It possessed a Class 2 primary [[Hyperdrive/Legends|hyperdrive]], with a Class 15 as backup in case the other failed. The [[Frigate/Legends|frigate]] had [[Sensor/Legends|sensors]], [[Deflector shield/Legends|deflector shields]], and a [[Navigation computer/Legends|navigation computer]] equipped. The armament of the ''Emperor's Will'' consisted of ten [[Turbolaser/Legends|turbolaser]] cannons, with five on each side of the frigate, as well as a [[Concussion missile/Legends|concussion missile]] launcher at the front of the ship. It had 50 concussion missiles on board, as well as enough [[Blaster gas/Legends|blaster gas]] for 1,000 shots from the [[Laser cannon/Legends|laser cannons]]. The frigate also possessed braking [[Engine/Legends|thrusters]] and six engines.<ref name="Prize" />

The [[Starship/Legends|ship]] had a cargo capacity of 100,000 [[Metric ton/Legends|metric tons]], and possessed enough consumables to last the ship's crew of 130 men and twenty [[Gunner/Legends|gunners]] for three [[Standard month/Legends|months]]. The ''Emperor's Will'' had room for a 300 passengers, which were usually [[Soldier/Legends|soldiers]], and could run on a skeleton crew of fifty crew and ten gunners if necessary. The frigate was as heavily [[Armor/Legends|armored]] as a [[Cruiser/Legends|cruiser]], and some of the interior of the ship could be reconfigured by the crew at the [[Bridge (starship)/Legends|bridge]] of the ship to frustrate [[Pirate/Legends|pirates]] and other boarders; the inside of the ''Emperor's Will'' also had anti-intruder defenses, some of which were [[Blaster/Legends|blaster]] slits and gas dispensers. The [[Cargo pod (Star Galleon)|cargo bay]] of the frigate was ejectable, and would automatically [[Hyperspace/Legends|jump]] to a position selected randomly from over hundreds of coordinates if the pod was released. The cargo bay pod emitted a [[Subspace transceiver/Legends|hypertransceiver]] signal, so it could be tracked by those the proper authorities. After a jump, the pod would stay at the new location for a random amount of [[Time/Legends|time]], before jumping into hyperspace again.<ref name="Prize" />

==History==
The ''Emperor's Will'' was used by the [[Imperial Taxation Bureau]] of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]]<ref name="Raid" /> sometime around the [[Standard year/Legends|year]] [[0 ABY/Legends|0 ABY]],<ref name="Date">{{FarOrbitDate}}</ref> at the time of the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]] between the Empire and the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Alliance to Restore the Republic]].<ref name="Orbit">''[[The Far Orbit Project]]''</ref> That year, the frigate departed from the [[Arkanis sector/Legends|Arkanis sector]]<ref name="Raid" /> on a trip to the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Esseles/Legends|Esseles]] in the [[Ringali Shell]] region, accompanied by the [[Imperial Navy/Legends|Imperial Navy's]] [[EF76 Nebulon-B escort frigate/Legends|EF76 Nebulon-B escort frigate]] ''[[Zaff Jendinpurg]]'' and carrying a cargo hold worth around 400 million [[Galactic Credit Standard/Legends|credits]], which was composed of precious metals, [[Mineral/Legends|minerals]], [[Spice/Legends|spices]], and valuable artwork,<ref name="Prize" /> all from taxes taken from primitive worlds in the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]] of [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]].<ref name="Orbit" /> Specifically, the cargo hold contained a range of gems that included [[Fervse|Bothan Glitterstones]], [[chrysopaz]]s, [[Crystalline vertex/Legends|crystalline vertices]], [[Diamond/Legends|diamonds]], [[Emerald/Legends|emeralds]], [[Rainbow gem|Gallinorean rainbow gems]], a [[Jasse heart]], [[Kuggerag/Legends|kuggerags]], a [[Nova crystal/Legends|nova crystal]], [[Quella stone|Quella gems]], [[Sapphire/Legends|sapphires]], and [[Sasho gem]]s; among the treasure was also a single [[Corusca gem/Legends|Corusca gem]] which had unique tracking properties. Additionally, a [[Jorallan opal]] necklace and a pair of matched sets of [[Lalmy'ashian pearl]] necklaces and earrings were also carried by the ''Emperor's Will''. As for spices, the cargo contained quantities of [[Andris/Legends|Andris]], [[Carsunum/Legends|Carsunum]], and [[ryll kor]]. The frigate's cargo weighed far less than the ''Emperor's Will''{{'s}} maximum cargo capacity, and, at that time, the ship was also carrying a [[Company/Legends|company]] of Imperial [[Stormtrooper/Legends|stormtroopers]].<ref name="Prize" />

{{RPGseed}}
[[File:EmperorsWillCargoHoldLaunch-TheFarOrbitProject.jpg|thumb|left|200px|The ''Emperor's Will'' launches its cargo hold.]]
On its non-stop journey through hyperspace, where it was out of communication the whole time, the ''Emperor's Will'' was dragged back into [[Realspace/Legends|realspace]] suddenly near the [[Ringali Nebula/Legends|Ringali Nebula]], alongside its escort. The reason for the event turned out to be a couple of [[Asteroid/Legends|asteroids]] that had been dragged into the frigate's path by the EF76 ''[[Far Orbit]]'', a [[Privateer/Legends|privateervessel]] for the Alliance; the ''Far Orbit'' had learned of the ''Emperor's Will''{{'s}} route after some of its crew had [[Mission to Brentaal IV|obtained]] a [[Datacard/Legends|datacard]] containing that information from an Alliance [[Unidentified Rebel waiter|contact]] on the world of [[Brentaal IV/Legends|Brentaal IV]].<ref name="Prize" />

The ''Far Orbit'', under the helm of [[Captain/Legends|Captain]] [[Dhas Fenoep Vedij]], [[Capture of the Emperor's Will|attacked]] the ''Emperor's Will''{{'s}} escort, which had been damaged by the abrupt drop out of hyperspace. As both Imperial ships had been completely surprised by the sudden change of events, the ''Star Galleon''-class frigate's escort was destroyed despite attempting to get its full complement of [[TIE series/Legends|TIE Series]] [[Starfighter/Legends|starfighters]] launched so that they could attack the ''Far Orbit''. The ''Emperor's Will'' then engaged the ''Far Orbit'', firing its concussion missile launcher, before trying to retreat from the battle and jump into hyperspace once again. The attempt, however, left the ''Emperor's Will''{{'s}} unarmed aft open to attack, which the ''Far Orbit'' capitalized on. The damage dealt by the privateering vessel prevented the Imperial frigate from jumping, leaving it to re-engage the enemy, and the [[Emperor's Will's captain|captain]] of the ''Emperor's Will'' tried to attack the ''Far Orbit'' on its side, where it was more vulnerable. In the end, the captain of the Imperial ship, realizing that he had lost the battle, made one final attempt to save his cargo by sending the ship's cargo pod away in order to deprive the privateers of it.<ref name="Prize" />

Explosive charges split the hull apart across the long axis, releasing the cargo pod, which tried to escape, to no avail. The ''Far Orbit'' captured the pod, and stole the treasures contained within. As a result of the capture of the ''Emperor's Will''{{'s}} cargo, the Imperial captain [[Vocis Kenit]]&mdash;who was in charge of tracking the ''Far Orbit''&mdash;was [[Death/Legends|executed]] by [[Emperor/Legends|Emperor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]] himself for failing to stop the frigate. In fact, the Corusca gem hidden away in the cargo hold the privateers had captured possessed unique tracking values that Kenit wished to use to catch the ''Far Orbit'' with, but the secret of the gem died with him.<ref name="Prize" />
{{Endgame}}

==Commanders and crew==
The ''Emperor's Will'' was under the command of a captain at the time of its encounter with the ''Far Orbit''. The Imperial frigate was crewed by a 150 people, including twenty [[Gunner/Legends|gunners]]. At skeleton crew, the ship could run with fifty crew and ten gunners.<ref name="Prize" />

==Behind the scenes==
The ''Emperor's Will'' was first mentioned in [[1998]]'s ''[[The Far Orbit Project]]'', by [[Timothy S. O'Brien]]. It was mentioned in some of the adventure scenarios contained within the book, and also appeared in ''[[The Grand Prize]]'', the last of those scenarios. ''The Far Orbit Project'' was a supplement to [[West End Games]]'s ''[[Star Wars: The Roleplaying Game]]'' and had the same theme of the previous publication ''[[Pirates & Privateers]]'', as it followed the privateering vessel ''Far Orbit''. The frigate served in the final adventure scenario that was given to the ''Far Orbit'' as the goal of the latter vessel. The capture of the ''Emperor's Will'' is the suggested spot where the ''Far Orbit'' finishes its campaign in the Ringali Shell.

In the battle with the privateering vessel, the ''Emperor's Will'' can be disabled by the privateers, as they do not want the treasure to be destroyed, in numerous ways. Precision fire against the engines, [[Ion cannon/Legends|ion cannon]] fire against the main hull if the ''Far Orbit'' has acquired those, or even attaching itself to the Imperial frigate with its [[Tractor beam/Legends|tractor beams]] to prevent it from escaping would work, though the ultimate path is up to the players. The players can also choose to board the ''Emperor's Will'', though the stormtroopers will resist; ''The Far Orbit Project'' mentions that if the gamemaster wishes to kill Vedij off, the boarding of the ''Emperor's Will'' would be an ideal place, as long as the death is heroic. The adventure scenario contradicts itself on how many passengers the ''Emperor's Will'' could hold, as it said the amounts of both 150 and 300. However, this article assumes the correct number is 300, as it is the number backed up more.

The gamemaster can calculate the total value of the treasure in order to adjust it to personal and player preference, as well as the size of the roleplaying campaign. They can also add additional rare items to the cargo hold of the ''Emperor's Will'' if they want to prolong the ''Far Orbit''{{'s}} campaign against the Empire.
